title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 417
paragraphs: As soon as the Ichthyophagoi arrived at Cambyses from Elephantine, he sent them to the Ethiopians, instructing them what they should say and giving them gifts to carry: a purple garment, a collar of twisted gold with bracelets, an alabaster box of perfumed ointment, and a jar of palm wine. Now these Ethiopians to whom Cambyses was sending them are said to be the tallest and most handsome of all men; and besides other customs they are reported to differ from other men in, there is this particular one regarding their royal power — whichever of their nation they judge to be the tallest and to have strength in proportion to his stature, that man they appoint to reign over them.
